{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared for:** Customer (internal)  
**Subject:** Playbook review findings, proposed redlines and walk-away items  
**Findings reviewed:** 18 (10 compliant, 5 deviations, 3 missing)

---

## Executive summary

The risk-allocation core of this Agreement is in good shape. Liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), the licence grant (§ 13), audit rights (§ 22), auto-renewal and price uplift (§ 8), warranties (§ 19) and Vendor insurance (§ 18) all meet our preferred positions, and several provisions are better than our benchmark (mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; hosted-Service conformity for the full subscription term; renewal-reminder mechanic that extends our opt-out deadline; uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection, security and indemnity).

The problems are concentrated in the commercial-lock-in and exit provisions, and in one significant omission. **There is no indemnification clause at all** — Section 20 is simply absent, even though §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all cross-refer to it. Separately, § 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year, three-year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights"; § 7.2 imposes a disclose-and-match obligation that operates as both de facto exclusivity and a Customer-side MFN; § 12.4 imposes a 24-month one-way no-hire and an undefined-scope non-compete on us; there is no termination-for-convenience right; and there is no transition-assistance or data-return obligation on exit. Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which is outside our accepted list and contradicts § 28.2 (New York County courts).

The draft is also internally inconsistent in ways that help us in negotiation: § 12.3 records that Customer has made **no** exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment, which directly contradicts §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4. We should press that inconsistency rather than argue each term in isolation. We also note the service-level exhibit referenced in § 2.2 is not in the document (so we cannot confirm service credits run in our favour), no Section 11 exists despite the cross-reference in § 16.5, and § 14.2's "revocable, non-transferable" Deliverable licence sits awkwardly against §§ 13.2–13.3 and 14.3.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2, 21.3, 18.2) | Meets preferred position; mutual cap, uncapped Excluded Claims. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Meets preferred position in full; no change-of-control trigger against us. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 | No LD, penalty or exit charge; § 27.3 terminates "without penalty". § 2.1 exposure handled under MINCOMMIT. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.3) | Meets preferred position; § 14.2 tension addressed under IP. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2–22.3) | Meets preferred position on every material term. |
| Medium | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 14.2 | Vendor owns all Deliverables; we get only a revocable, term-limited licence. Fails the fallback. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-way 24-month no-hire of any Vendor employee, no carve-outs. Walk-away territory. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, CPI/3% uplift cap. Better than preferred on reminders. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.2 (with §§ 19.1, 19.3–19.5) | Meets or exceeds preferred; disclaimer limited to implied warranties. |
| Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | De facto exclusivity/ROFR across all Services for the full term, no performance exit. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction; outside accepted list and conflicts with § 28.2. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | No Section 20 in document (see § 19.5; cross-refs at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5) | No Vendor IP or other indemnity anywhere. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 (with § 18.2) | CGL, E&O, USD 5M cyber/privacy, workers' comp; term plus one year. |
| Low | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | Open-ended Customer-side disclose-and-match duty; no product, duration or comparability limits. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | USD 2,000,000/year for three years, take-or-pay, "without reduction or termination rights". Walk-away territory. |
| Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | Term plus 24 months, "any product or service", "any territory", no carve-outs. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9 (§ 9.3 quoted); § 2.1 | No Customer convenience right in a three-year term locked by § 2.1. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 10.2 (with § 16.5) | No migration assistance, data export or certified deletion; § 16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11. |

---

## Walk-away items

These sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and, unless resolved, should not be signed:

1. **No indemnification (absent Section 20).** No Vendor IP infringement indemnity or any other defence obligation. We propose inserting a new Section 20 at the preferred position: Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard notice, control and cooperation procedure; customary exclusions and procure–modify–replace–refund remedies at 20.5 (which also cures the dangling cross-reference in § 9.3); and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. No super-cap is needed because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims.
2. **§ 2.1 take-or-pay (MINCOMMIT).** A three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year commitment with no reduction or termination rights. We propose payment only for Services ordered or used; the fallback (a commitment for the current 12-month term only, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised) is available if Vendor needs a floor.
3. **§ 7.2 disclose-and-match (EXCLUSIVITY and MFN).** Independently breaches both rules: it is an exclusivity/ROFR on our sourcing and an open-ended Customer-side MFN. Preferred remedy is deletion of the Customer-side obligation; any Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would be retained.
4. **§ 12.4 non-compete (NONCOMPETE).** Term plus 24 months, undefined scope and territory, no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. Preferred remedy is deletion; a narrowed fallback can be offered in comment.
5. **§ 12.4 no-hire (NOSOLICIT).** One-way, 24 months, all Vendor employees, no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. Fallback is a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with those carve-outs and no no-hire element.
6. **§ 28.1 Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue (GOVLAW).** Outside the accepted list and in conflict with § 28.2. We propose New York law and the state and federal courts in New York County; § 28.3's pre-suit escalation preserving urgent relief is unaffected.
7. **No termination for convenience (T4C).** No Customer convenience right in a multi-year term expressly locked by § 2.1. We propose a new § 9.4 giving Customer 30 days' notice convenience termination with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and a conforming carve-out in § 2.1 so the right is effective. Vendor likewise has no convenience right, which is consistent with our position.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the five deviations and three gaps above. Two proposed edits did not pass automated verification and require manual drafting before the redline goes out: the **§ 12.4 non-solicit narrowing** and the **new § 9.4 convenience-termination right** (including the conforming § 2.1 carve-out).
2. **Lead with the § 12.3 inconsistency.** Vendor's own acknowledgement that Customer has made no exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment contradicts §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4. Framing these as drafting conflicts to be conformed to § 12.3 is a cleaner path than five separate commercial negotiations.
3. **Fix the missing and dangling references.** Confirm whether an indemnity was intended and dropped in assembly (§§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5 all assume one), and resolve § 16.5's reference to a non-existent Section 11.
4. **Request the missing service-level exhibit** referenced in § 2.2 so we can confirm service credits and the § 9.3 "repeatedly misses a critical service level" trigger operate in our favour.
5. **Deliverables ownership (§ 14.2).** Seek Customer ownership with an express Vendor assignment, preserving Vendor's retained Vendor Technology rights under § 14.3; the fallback is a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables. Note the tension with §§ 13.2–13.3 and 14.3, which currently cover Vendor Technology only and do not cure § 14.2.
6. **Add exit protections (new § 10.3):** up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion thereafter, with a routine-backup and legal-retention carve-out consistent with § 16.5.
7. **Do not reopen the compliant provisions.** Sections 8, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22 and 24 meet our positions or better; raising them risks trading away favourable terms."}
